title: What is Model Context Protocol?
description: Get a clear introduction to MCP, the problem it solves, and how it compares to traditional API patterns for AI backends.

blocks.text: Model Context Protocol is an open standard for connecting AI systems to external tools, data sources, and prompt templates. It was designed to solve a recurring problem: AI clients need to discover and use backend capabilities without custom integrations for every API.

blocks.title: Pain points in backend AI integration
items: Every AI client needs custom wrappers around each backend API.
Tool descriptions drift out of sync with actual API behavior.
Authentication, transport, and schema details differ for every integration.
Prompt templates and context retrieval require bespoke code.

blocks.title: Core primitives
items: **Resources** — structured data exposed by the server, such as a document, schema, or record.
**Prompts** — reusable prompt templates with parameters the client can fill.
**Tools** — callable functions the client can invoke, with typed inputs and outputs.
**Transports** — stdio for local communication and HTTP/SSE for remote servers.

blocks.title: MCP server concept in C#
blocks.content: An MCP server registers tools, resources, and prompts, then exposes them over a transport.

blocks.title: MCP is not just for chatbots
blocks.text: MCP servers can serve agents, IDEs, automation platforms, and internal tools. Any client that speaks the protocol can consume your backend capabilities.

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: MCP is an open protocol for AI-ready backend integration.
It replaces bespoke wrappers with standard resources, prompts, and tools.
C# backends can host MCP servers that wrap existing business logic.
blocks.takeaway: MCP turns your backend into an AI-friendly service without abandoning the APIs and databases you already have.
